description: This topic deals with the calculation of additional amounts earned on investments or paid on borrowings. Mastering basic formulas, effective percentage methods, and shortcut tricks is essential for quick pattern recognition and time-saving in competitive exams.

sections.title: Basic Terminology and Concepts
sections.description: Understanding the core variables involved in interest calculation is the foundation for solving any related problem.

key_concepts.explanation: The initial sum of money that is borrowed or invested.
The percentage of the principal charged or earned over a specific period, typically expressed per annum (p.a.).
The total duration for which the money is borrowed or invested, usually measured in years.
The total sum of the Principal and the accumulated Interest at the end of the time period.

sections.title: Advanced Problem-Solving Strategies
sections.description: Use these actionable steps and advanced methods to bypass complex calculations and solve problems efficiently.

steps.title: Effective Percentage Method (for 2 years CI)
steps.detail: Instead of using the standard formula, calculate the effective CI rate for 2 years using $R_{effective} = R + R +  rac{R 	imes R}{100}$. For example, if R=10%, CI rate = $10 + 10 + 1 = 21\%$. Then simply calculate 21% of the Principal.

steps.title: Ratio / Scaling Method
steps.detail: If a sum grows to $A_1$ in $T$ years and $A_2$ in $2T$ years at CI, the principal $P$ can be found using the relation $P =  rac{A_1 	imes A_1}{A_2}$ because CI follows a Geometric Progression.

steps.title: The Tree Method for CI
steps.detail: For multi-year CI problems without formulas, break down the interest visually. Year 1: $X$ (which is $R\%$ of $P$). Year 2: $X$ + $Y$ (where $Y$ is $R\%$ of $X$). Year 3: $X$ + $2Y$ + $Z$ (where $Z$ is $R\%$ of $Y$). This is highly effective for solving 'difference' problems.
